headline: audit/ai-v3-hybrid-vs-hard-9050-headline.json

phaseDecisionTotals.note: 16858 hybrid decisions are not split by phase. Key decisions exist only for the 109 losses, at most 8 per game, ranked toward extra-draw and the anomaly flags. Those 680 rows are not the phase mix.

start.association: Every win and every loss used extraDraw. Per-turn rates are close. This record does not show a missed start action that separates wins from losses.

freshSample.scope: 6 retained loss snapshots, not all start decisions

move.association: No move-phase total exists. One position cannot rank this phase.

attack.storedSignal: per-own-turn attack counts. Attack declarations were not snapshotted.
attack.association: Losses record fewer attacks per own turn. Five white-sword losses never attack. The record has no attacker-choice log, so a wrong-attacker claim is not available.

pending.storedSignal: defender-lethal flags and their snapshots. Discard, trigger and effect choices were not retained.
pending.association: All 30 lethal marks are in losses. That is an association. The one-step block result does not prove those 30 passes caused the 109 losses.

whiteSecondAnomalies.note: Fewer front plays and more thin-front energy sit in the main phase, which already uses hard-search-2. Association only.

lethal.score: Every original block candidate is -100000. The pass is -90000. terminalValue returns -90000 when the match is unfinished and own life is 0, and -100000 when the match has finished as a loss.
lethal.oneStepMeaning: Dispatching each legal block on a clone keeps own life above 0 and does not open a life trigger. Impact is 0, so a block that loses the battle still does not remove a life. When blocker BP is not strictly higher, the blocker leaves. Only 3 positions have a strictly higher blocker, so neither character leaves. The pass action returns with life unchanged and pending attack-life-target. The life card and its trigger were not read.
lethal.freshSearchNote: Fresh 48/40 searches are not the original 40ms decisions. Hard passes on 28 of 30. Fresh v3 passes on 26 and blocks on 4, so 4 fresh v3 choices differ from the recorded pass.

examples.why: 已驗證的原始致命阻擋。一步結算後，BP 4000 的阻擋讓生命停在 3–1，衝擊是 0。通過停在 attack-life-target，生命還沒扣。原始 v3 把阻擋評成 -100000、通過評成 -90000。
已驗證的薄前線高 BP 能源。這手在主階段，原始來源是 hard-search-2。用來對照 v3 與 hard，不把它重算成原始 40ms。
已驗證的前四回合有合法高 BP 突襲卻放上能源。原始來源同樣是 hard-search-2。

A.route: main hard, attack hard, other lanes v3
A.evidence: Losses have fewer stored attacks per own turn (338/724 versus 390/657) and 5 white-sword losses never attack. No attack-declaration snapshot exists, so v3 and hard were not compared on the same attack.
A.downside: Attack volume is an association. Adding hard to every attack decision spends the 48/40 budget on a lane with no measured disagreement.
A.scope: Every attack declaration. Pending during attack would stay v3.

B.route: main hard, pending hard, other lanes v3
B.evidence: The 30 lethal marks are the only retained pending weakness, and they are all in losses. On those same verified positions a fresh hard search still passes 28 times and blocks 2. The original pass-versus-block scores are a v3 terminal-value gap. settleLife already tried to prefer the lived block and did not raise win rate, so it stays off.
B.downside: Routing all pending to hard would change discards, triggers and effect choices that were not retained. The fresh hard query does not show that hard blocks these lethal attacks.

C.route: main hard, start and move hard, other lanes v3
C.evidence: extraDraw occurs in all 91 wins and all 109 losses. On 6 retained loss snapshots, fresh hard chooses next while the original v3 choice was extraDraw. Move has 1 retained decision.
C.downside: The start sample is six loss snapshots. Wins use extraDraw at a similar rate, so skipping it is not a measured gain against hard-search-2.

recommendation.reason: None of A, B or C has enough evidence to be the single next A/B. B is the closest label for the lethal marks, and the fresh hard query answers it: hard also passes. A has no same-position attack comparison. C has a six-snapshot start disagreement that does not separate the 91 wins from the 109 losses. The shared block evaluation remains the clearest anomaly, and the previous settleLife test is not a reason to turn that switch back on.

informationGaps: Hybrid decision totals are not stored by phase. 16858 is the only decision count.
Snapshots and key decisions were kept only for losses, and only for ranked flags, at most 8 per game.
Wins have no local snapshots, so v3 and hard were not asked on winning positions.
Discard, life-trigger resolution and effect choices were not retained.
The pass continuation stops at attack-life-target. Life cards and triggers were not opened, so a trigger save is unknown. End-of-game life 0 is not attributed to that one pass.
Fresh searches use a new 40ms clock. They are labeled separately from the recorded live choice.
Move-phase quality cannot be ranked from one decision.
